exact_relations: Angular momentum per unit mass is r u_theta.
For the added velocity at fixed r, its radial angular-momentum transport factor is w_r(r w_theta)=r w_r w_theta.
Case A: w_r=+a>0 and w_theta=+b>0, so w_r w_theta=ab>0 and r w_r w_theta=rab>0.
Case B: w_r=-a<0 and w_theta=-b<0, so w_r w_theta=ab>0 and r w_r w_theta=rab>0.
The simultaneous sign reversal (w_r,w_theta) maps to (-w_r,-w_theta) and leaves w_r w_theta unchanged.
The r-theta component of equation (7.23) is C_rtheta(w)=double-average(w_r w_theta).
derivation: The source defines angular momentum per unit mass as r u_theta.
Multiplying this quantity by the radial added-velocity component w_r gives the local radial transport factor r w_r w_theta.
Because the displayed radius obeys r>0, multiplication by r does not change the sign.
Therefore both displayed sign pairs have the same positive outward angular-momentum flux factor.

For the separately labeled shared-cosine special case, w_r=s a cos(phi) and w_theta=s b cos(phi), where s is +1 or -1 and the angular frequency is a nonzero integer. The normalized angular average is a b times the average of cos(phi)^2, namely ab/2>0. This is a bridge to the first component of equation (7.23), not a drawing of the pulse field.
hypotheses: the two displayed component signs are paired as (+,+) or (-,-)
for the covariance bridge only: a shared cosine phase with nonzero integer angular frequency and normalized angular averaging
mathematical_binding.units: The source passage specifies no numerical units. The displayed factor has dimensions [radius] times [velocity]^2; only its sign is asserted.
mathematical_binding.projection_or_section_statement: This is component extraction followed by a scalar product map, not a geometric section or spatial projection. It suppresses w_z, position, pulse support, phase structure, profiles, amplitude scale, and the full solution.

claim_displayed: At fixed r>0, outward radial motion paired with a positive azimuthal surplus and inward radial motion paired with a negative azimuthal deficit both make r w_r w_theta positive; simultaneous reversal of both component signs leaves the product unchanged.

caption: Exact sign/product diagram at one fixed radius r>0. In the local cylindrical basis, w_r=+a and w_theta=+b give r w_r w_theta=rab>0; reversing both components gives w_r=-a and w_theta=-b and the same positive product. Equation (7.23) uses w_r w_theta as the r-theta covariance component. The arrows encode signs and basis directions only; they do not depict pulse geometry, support, paths, profiles, magnitudes, or the full three-dimensional solution.
long_text_alternative: An exact two-case sign diagram at one fixed cylindrical radius r>0. The orientation key says that positive e_r points away from the axis and positive e_theta is the chosen positive tangent direction. Case A shows an outward radial arrow labeled w_r=+a>0 and a positive azimuthal arrow labeled w_theta=+b>0. Their product is (+a)(+b)=ab>0, and multiplying by r>0 gives r w_r w_theta=rab>0. Case B shows an inward radial arrow labeled w_r=-a<0 and a negative azimuthal arrow labeled w_theta=-b<0. Their product is (-a)(-b)=ab>0, and the same multiplication gives rab>0. A lower box states that simultaneous sign reversal leaves the product fixed. A covariance note states that the r-theta component is the double average of w_r w_theta, and that a shared cosine phase with nonzero integer angular frequency has angular average ab/2>0. A scope note says that arrow directions encode component signs and basis orientation only, not pulse geometry, paths, profiles, magnitudes, support, or the full solution.
